questions.q: Which is the eco-friendly choice?
questions.n: Clay is natural, durable and recyclable; the others carry toxins or petroleum.

questions.q: A collar tie between opposing rafters is placed in the:
questions.n: Collar ties sit high; rafter ties sit low.

questions.q: Re-roofing a hospital wing with patients sensitive to fumes, choose:
questions.n: EPDM goes on cold, with no hot asphalt fumes.

questions.q: Where the two sloping top chords of a roof meet at the top is the:
questions.n: The ridge is the highest horizontal line of a roof.

questions.q: A light, bitumen-based roofing with moderate wind resistance is:
questions.n: Asphalt shingles are bitumen products, light and fairly wind-resistant when properly nailed.

questions.q: Sag rods belong to the:
questions.n: Sag rods keep purlins from sagging down the slope.

questions.q: For the same plan, which roof needs the most gutter length?
questions.n: Hips have eaves on all four sides.

questions.q: A long-span training hall needs a very light, factory-painted, UV-stable roofing cut to full length so there are no end laps. Which material?
questions.n: Only metal sheet offers long structural spans, factory finishes and cut-to-length supply together.

questions.q: The vertical center member of a king-post truss is the:
questions.n: The king post runs from apex to tie beam.

questions.q: The surest way to avoid galvanic corrosion on a metal roof is:
o: Fasteners and accessories of the same metal as the sheet
questions.n: Dissimilar metals in contact with moisture corrode.

questions.q: The installation mistake most often behind leaks in GI roofs is:
o: Leaving out a ridge vent screen
questions.n: Screws missing the purlin, overtightened, or placed without washers open leak paths.

questions.q: Small overlapping units laid in courses, each lapping the one below, are:
questions.n: Shingles shed water by lapping.

questions.q: The most common roof covering on Philippine houses is:
questions.n: Corrugated galvanized iron dominates local housing.

questions.q: Cheap, local, naturally insulating, but needing regular replacement: the traditional rural roof is:
questions.n: Thatch is renewable and cool but short-lived.

questions.q: A rigid triangulated frame of chords, posts and webs used for roofs is a:
questions.n: Trusses carry roof loads through axial forces.

questions.q: Which roofing is cheapest per square meter?
questions.n: Plain corrugated sheet is the economy option.

questions.q: The most common roof form is the:
questions.n: Simple, cheap and good at shedding water.

questions.q: A simple hip roof on a rectangular plan has how many valleys?
questions.n: Valleys only occur at inside corners, as in L-shaped plans.

questions.q: Why does long-span metal roofing save money over the life of the roof?
o: Fewer end laps means fewer leak points
questions.n: Continuous sheets eliminate the end laps where leaks start.

questions.q: On a house roof, C-purlins are commonly spaced about:
questions.n: About 0.60 m suits typical long-span sheets.

questions.q: Corrugated roofing fastened through the crest (high rib) is correct practice when:
o: Never; fasten only through the valleys
It's only a temporary canvas roof
The screw lands on a purlin and has a sealing washer
questions.n: Crest fixing keeps the hole out of the water path; self-drilling screws with EPDM washers are standard.

questions.q: Where a roof slope butts against a parapet or firewall, the flashing used is:
questions.n: Apron flashing turns up the wall and laps over the sheet.

questions.q: On a wooden roof frame, purlins are carried by the:
questions.n: Purlins span across the rafters.

questions.q: Raised interlocking ribs, hidden clips, panels running unbroken from ridge to eave, and free thermal movement. Which roof system?
questions.n: Standing-seam panels lock at raised seams above the water line, with no exposed fasteners.

questions.q: Hoop buildings are made of:
questions.n: Hoop houses are tensioned fabric over steel bows.

questions.q: C-purlins are commonly sold in lengths of:
questions.n: 6 m lengths are standard stock.

questions.q: Thickest metal roofing sheet commonly available locally:
questions.n: Local long-span sheets top out around 0.70 mm.

questions.q: Half trusses (jack trusses) are used at the:
questions.n: They fill the triangular hip.

questions.q: A seaside house is on a budget and must ride out typhoons. Which roof covering?
questions.n: Metal sheets are economical and, well fastened, resist uplift better than tiles or shingles.

questions.q: The heaviest roof covering in this list is:
questions.n: Natural slate is dense stone and needs a stout frame.

questions.q: A roof built up from alternating plies of felt and hot bitumen is:
questions.n: BUR is a multi-ply bituminous membrane.

questions.q: Rolled roofing should not go on a roof flatter than about:
questions.n: Below that slope, roll roofing laps can't shed water.

questions.q: In local truss carpentry, the horizontal bottom chord that also ties the rafters is the:
questions.n: Tirante is the tie beam; kilo is the king post.

questions.q: Of these roof coverings, the most expensive is:
questions.n: Copper costs far more than steel or concrete roofing.

questions.q: Gaps are left between polycarbonate sheets and around their fixings to allow for:
questions.n: Polycarbonate expands a lot with heat and buckles if restrained.

questions.q: For a low-pitched roof in the tropics, the practical choice is:
questions.n: Tiles and thatch need steep pitches to shed water.

questions.q: A shallow-pitch roof in a windy, wet area needs hidden fasteners, long ridge-to-eave runs with no end laps, and room for thermal movement. Specify:
o: Corrugated sheets screwed through the valleys
questions.n: Standing seam uses concealed clips and continuous panels, so there are few leak paths.

questions.q: DPWH specs (D.O. 03 s. 2018) call for gutters, valleys, flashings and ridge rolls fabricated from which gauge pre-painted sheet?
questions.n: Item 1014.2.1 sets gauge 24 for these roof accessories.
